Network egress to UNC6508 C2 infrastructure (23.169.65.49) AICommand & Control High
Egress / DNS / proxy detections for the published UNC6508 C2 IP 23.169.65.49. Pivots on any process initiating the connection so analysts can immediately see whether the caller was a REDCap host, a domain controller, or an admin workstation. Rationale: Single-IOC pivot using the C2 IP published by GTIG. Multi-source so the same UC catches REDCap-host beacons (DeviceNetworkEvents), perimeter firewall hits (CommonSecurityLog), and inbound login traffic from the IP back to AWS-hosted REDCap mirrors (VPC Flow).
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform validating the IOC by reaching the IP
  • Researcher's sandbox calling out to the attacker infrastructure
  • Vendor scan/probe against the IP from a security tool
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName has_any ("sandbox","detlab","ir-vm") or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("thunderhunt.exe","misp-tools"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — identify the initiating process and host. If the caller is a REDCap server, treat as confirmed UNC6508 compromise; if it's a researcher VM, validate the segmentation. Capture full pcap if available. 2) Contain — block 23.169.65.49 at perimeter + EDR network containment; isolate the calling host; pull memory before reboot. 3) Hunt — sweep DNS for PTR / passive-DNS lookups of the same IP, pivot to neighbouring /24, look back 24 months on this IP (UNC6508 has been active since Sept 2023), and check Workspace admin audit on the same calendar day for rule creation (UC1) which is the typical post-C2 action.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where RemoteIP == "23.169.65.49"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, Protocol,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d) | where DestinationIP == "23.169.65.49" or SourceIP == "23.169.65.49" | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication),
  (ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d) | where DstIpAddr == "23.169.65.49" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url),
  (ImDnsActivity | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d) | where DstIpAddr == "23.169.65.49" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DnsQuery, DstIpAddr),
  (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(180d) | where cIP == "23.169.65.49" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csUriStem, csUserAgent, scStatus)

Trojanized REDCap PHP system-file modification (INFINITERED install) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the INFINITERED install primitive: modification or replacement of REDCap's own PHP system files (login page, upgrade scripts) on the server. Article specifies the malware trojanizes REDCap files so each upgrade reinjects the code — first-seen modification of REDCap PHP outside an apt/yum/composer parent is the canonical signal. Rationale: Article: 'trojanizes REDCap's own system files' and 'hijacks the upgrade process so each new REDCap version reinjects the code'. The login page being modified is also explicit ('harvests usernames and passwords from the login page'). Restricting to .php under /redcap/ AND excluding package-manager / web-server parents is the tightest filter without naming specific source files Google didn't publish.
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1554 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate REDCap version upgrade run by an admin via a console/SSH session (parent will be bash/zsh, not apt — must whitelist by host + change ticket)
  • Custom REDCap plugin development on a non-prod instance
  • Configuration-management tooling (Ansible/Puppet/Chef) deploying REDCap patches
  • DevOps pipeline copying files via rsync/scp during deploy
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("redcap-deploy","ansible","puppet") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("ansible-playbook","puppet apply","chef-client"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — compare the modified PHP file against the upstream REDCap release SHA256 (Vanderbilt publishes per-version manifests). If hash diverges and there's no active change ticket, treat as INFINITERED. Capture file contents before remediation — INFINITERED encrypts harvested credentials into local DB tables, you need the encryption key from the binary. 2) Contain — isolate the server, snapshot, take REDCap offline, scope which DB tables INFINITERED wrote to (likely a fresh table with bytea/blob columns), preserve them, then reimage from a pre-Sept-2023 known-good snapshot. 3) Hunt — sweep every external REDCap install in the org for the same path mods; rotate every credential ever entered into the login page over the compromise window; cross-check Workspace admin audit (UC1) and C2 IP egress (UC3) for follow-on activity.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(180d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/redcap/","\\redcap\\","/redcap_v","\\redcap_v")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("apt","apt-get","dpkg","yum","dnf","rpm","composer","php-fpm","php","git","tar","unzip","gunzip","sshd","rsync","msiexec.exe","trustedinstaller.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/lib/apt" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/bin/dpkg"
| extend SuspiciousFile = iff(FileName matches regex @"(?i)(login|index|init_functions|system|database|upgrade|home)\.php$", true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, SuspiciousFile,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by SuspiciousFile desc, Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(180d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/redcap/","\\redcap\\","/redcap_v","\\redcap_v")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".php"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("apt","apt-get","dpkg","yum","dnf","rpm","composer","php-fpm","php","git","tar","unzip","sshd","rsync","msiexec.exe","trustedinstaller.exe")
| extend SuspiciousFile = iff(TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)(login|index|init_functions|system|database|upgrade|home)\.php$", true, false)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, SuspiciousFile, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by SuspiciousFile desc, TimeGenerated desc

Bulk Gmail export / Takeout immediately following Workspace admin rule change AIActions on Objectives Medium
Correlates UNC6508's two-stage exfiltration shape: an admin creates or modifies a Workspace mail-routing/content-compliance rule, then within hours a bulk Gmail export or Google Takeout is initiated. Either event alone is low-signal; the pairing is high. Rationale: Article: 'stealing sensitive research and defense email' over 26+ months via the rule — once exfil is established, attackers commonly also pull historic archives to capture pre-rule traffic. Correlating rule-change → Takeout/export by the same admin object within 7d narrows the FP space dramatically. Sentinel/Falcon/Datadog left blank: Workspace audit doesn't natively land there.
ATT&CKT1114.002 T1020 T1567.002
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate eDiscovery / legal-hold workflow where compliance officer enables a content rule then exports
  • User offboarding playbook that creates a forwarding rule and then exports the user's mailbox
  • Migration to a new tenant that combines routing changes and bulk export
  • Disaster-recovery archive process triggered after an admin policy change
Suppression filter
| where not (RuleAdmin has_any ("ediscovery","legal","compliance","hr-offboarding") and ExportData has_any ("legal-hold-case","offboarding-archive","ediscovery-export"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the rule definition and the export job parameters. Inspect destination of the Takeout (which mailbox/user, where the archive is being delivered) and whether the keywords overlap with UNC6508's collection priorities (geo-strategic, defense, biotech, AI/UAV, offensive cyber). 2) Contain — pause/cancel any in-flight Takeout jobs, delete the rule, revoke the admin session, lock the admin account, block the Takeout destination if external. 3) Hunt — pivot on the admin object: every prior session, every prior rule edit, every prior export. Check whether the IP and user-agent match historical legitimate admin sessions or look like a fresh attacker stack.
let lookback = 30d;
let WindowDays = 7d;
let RuleChanges = CloudAppEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
  | where Application has_any ("Google Workspace","G Suite","Gmail")
  | where IsAdminOperation == true
  | where ActionType has_any ("CHANGE_EMAIL_SETTING","CREATE_EMAIL_MONITOR","CONTENT_COMPLIANCE","CREATE_GMAIL_SETTING","EmailRouting")
  | project RuleTime = Timestamp, RuleAdmin = AccountDisplayName, RuleAdminObjectId = AccountObjectId, RuleAction = ActionType, RuleSrcIP = IPAddress, RuleData = tostring(RawEventData);
let Exports = CloudAppEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
  | where Application has_any ("Google Workspace","G Suite","Gmail","Google Takeout")
  | where ActionType has_any ("DOWNLOAD_USER_DATA","TAKEOUT","USER_TAKEOUT","DATA_EXPORT","GMAIL_RESERVED_KEYWORD_EXPORT","DataExport")
  | project ExportTime = Timestamp, ExportActor = AccountDisplayName, ExportActorObjectId = AccountObjectId, ExportAction = ActionType, ExportSrcIP = IPAddress, ExportData = tostring(RawEventData);
RuleChanges
| join kind=inner Exports on $left.RuleAdminObjectId == $right.ExportActorObjectId
| where ExportTime between (RuleTime .. RuleTime + WindowDays)
| extend DelayHours = datetime_diff('hour', ExportTime, RuleTime)
| project RuleTime, ExportTime, DelayHours, RuleAdmin, RuleSrcIP, ExportSrcIP, RuleAction, ExportAction, RuleData, ExportData
| order by RuleTime desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
let lookback = 30d;
let WindowDays = 7d;
let RuleChanges = CloudAppEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)

  | where IsAdminOperation == true

  | project RuleTime = TimeGenerated, RuleAdmin = AccountDisplayName, RuleAdminObjectId = AccountObjectId, RuleAction = ActionType, RuleSrcIP = IPAddress, RuleData = tostring(RawEventData);
let Exports = CloudAppEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
  | where Application has_any ("Google Workspace","G Suite","Gmail","Google Takeout")
  | where ActionType has_any ("DOWNLOAD_USER_DATA","TAKEOUT","USER_TAKEOUT","DATA_EXPORT","GMAIL_RESERVED_KEYWORD_EXPORT","DataExport")
  | project ExportTime = TimeGenerated, ExportActor = AccountDisplayName, ExportActorObjectId = AccountObjectId, ExportAction = ActionType, ExportSrcIP = IPAddress, ExportData = tostring(RawEventData);
RuleChanges
| join kind=inner Exports on $left.RuleAdminObjectId == $right.ExportActorObjectId
| where ExportTime between (RuleTime .. RuleTime + WindowDays)
| extend DelayHours = datetime_diff('hour', ExportTime, RuleTime)
| project RuleTime, ExportTime, DelayHours, RuleAdmin, RuleSrcIP, ExportSrcIP, RuleAction, ExportAction, RuleData, ExportData
| order by RuleTime desc

Anomalous HTTP cookie payload to REDCap endpoints (INFINITERED C2 channel) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the INFINITERED command channel described in the article — 'takes commands through HTTP cookies and runs on every page load'. Surfaces inbound HTTP requests to REDCap URLs with unusually long, high-entropy, or base64-looking Cookie headers from external IPs, which is the operator beacon shape. Rationale: Direct from article: INFINITERED 'acts as a backdoor, taking commands through HTTP cookies and running on every page load' against REDCap pages. Filters to /redcap/ paths and looks for the operator beacon characteristic: oversized cookies / base64 chunks > 200 chars, which exceed any legitimate REDCap session cookie. Tier is hunting because the threshold is heuristic and per-environment tuning of the length is expected.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1132.001 T1573
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate REDCap session with very large JWT/session blob (some SSO integrations emit 2-3 KB cookies)
  • Load-balancer sticky-session cookies stacked with REDCap session
  • Browser with many third-party cookies replaying to REDCap
  • Penetration-tester or automated DAST scanner fuzzing the cookie field
Response runbook
1) Triage — capture the full cookie payload, decode base64 segments, look for typed command structure (UNC6508 uses encrypted command bodies; pattern is repeated short cookies of similar length not full session blobs). Cross-check the source IP against UC3 (23.169.65.49). 2) Contain — block the source IP, isolate the REDCap host, capture memory + process list (the INFINITERED handler runs on every page load so it should be active), preserve web-server access logs. 3) Hunt — pull every request from the same source IP in the last 24 months, decode any other long-cookie patterns, sweep for INFINITERED hashes (UC2) on the host, and review Workspace admin audit (UC1) for downstream exfil rule activity.
let lookback = 14d;
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where RequestURL has "/redcap/" or DestinationServiceName has "redcap"
    | where isnotempty(RequestCookies)
    | extend CookieLen = strlen(RequestCookies)
    | where CookieLen > 512
    | extend HighEntropyB64 = iff(RequestCookies matches regex @"[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{200,}", true, false)
    | where HighEntropyB64 or CookieLen > 1024
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DeviceVendor, DestinationServiceName, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, CookieLen, HighEntropyB64, RequestCookies),
  (W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
    | where csUriStem has "/redcap/"
    | extend CookieLen = strlen(tostring(parse_json(tostring(pack_all())).csCookie)) // adjust if csCookie custom-mapped
    | where CookieLen > 512
    | project TimeGenerated, cIP, csUriStem, csUserAgent, scStatus, CookieLen)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

summariesonly=false | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*/redcap/*" OR Web.uri_path="*/redcap/*" by Web.src Web.dest Web.url Web.user_agent Web.http_method _time _raw | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rex field=_raw "(?i)Cookie:\s*(?<cookie_header>[^\r\n]+)" | eval cookie_len=len(cookie_header) | where cookie_len > 512 | eval looks_b64=if(match(cookie_header,"[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{200,}"),1,0) | where looks_b64=1 OR cookie_len > 1024 | table _time src dest url user_agent cookie_len cookie_header
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count

Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High

DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"

        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or SHA1 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or MD5 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86")

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Yeeth-disclosed malicious Jupyter VSIX extensions (ByteBinTools / ToolCraft / OLDev) · [LLM] UNK_DeadDrop Windows VBScript loader → cmd → code.exe --install-extension chain · Suspicious browser extension installation · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] UNK_DeadDrop / Contagious Interview C2 callback (23.137.105.75:5173 + Proofpoint domain set) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
VS Code (Code.exe) autorun spawning downloader/script — UNK_DeadDrop folderOpen abuse AIExploitation High
Hunts the Contagious Interview / UNK_DeadDrop tasks.json runOn:folderOpen technique, where simply opening a cloned repo in VS Code or Cursor triggers Code.exe to spawn a downloader, script interpreter, or encoded-PowerShell child. Combines the unusual parent (Code.exe) with high-signal child binaries / cmdline indicators of network fetch, base64, or LOLBin abuse. Rationale: Targets the article's central, novel TTP — VS Code tasks.json runOn:folderOpen abuse adopted by Contagious Interview since December 2025. Code.exe is rarely a parent of wscript/mshta/bitsadmin/certutil in a normal dev workstation; pairing parent=Code.exe with a LOLBin child or a shell carrying download/encoded markers is high-signal. Corroborated against Proofpoint's UNK_DeadDrop write-up referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1546 T1204.002 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Postinstall npm scripts that legitimately curl resources during dependency build
  • DevOps onboarding tasks that invoke certutil/bitsadmin from a VS Code terminal
  • PowerShell profile loaders launched by the integrated terminal (Invoke-Expression on profile import)
  • Cursor / VS Code Insiders test workloads using Net.WebClient for telemetry
  • Internal extension build steps that legitimately call DownloadFile against artifact servers
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--extensionDevelopmentPath","--extensionTestsPath")) // exclude VS Code extension authoring
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "npm " and ProcessCommandLine has "postinstall" and InitiatingProcessAccountName has "build") // CI build accounts
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on DeviceId — pull the InitiatingProcessCommandLine for Code.exe to find the workspace folder; check whether a .vscode/tasks.json or .githooks/pre-commit exists in that path, and grep its content for runOn:folderOpen, curl, or base64. 2) Contain: isolate the host via MDE, kill the Code.exe + child tree, block 23.137.105.75 and the campaign domain list at the proxy/DNS sink, and force credential rotation for any browser-stored wallets, GitHub PAT, npmrc tokens, and SSH keys on the host. 3) Hunt: pivot on the InitiatingProcessAccountObjectId to find every device that user opened the same repo on; query DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to 23.137.105.75:5173 and the Proofpoint domain list; search DeviceFileEvents for the three Yeeth VSIX names and for .githooks/pre-commit drops.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "code.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","regsvr32.exe","rundll32.exe","curl.exe","bash.exe","wsl.exe"))
   or (FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
       and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","DownloadFile","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","Invoke-WebRequest","Net.WebClient","Invoke-Expression","IEX ","curl ","wget ","bitsadmin","certutil -urlcache","Set-MpPreference"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Child = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\Code.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (NewProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\mshta.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\bitsadmin.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\certutil.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\regsvr32.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\rundll32.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\curl.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\bash.exe")
   or ((NewProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith @"\pwsh.exe") and (CommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","DownloadFile","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand","Invoke-WebRequest","Net.WebClient","curl ","wget ","bitsadmin","certutil -urlcache")))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Contagious Interview repo autoexec artifacts written (.vscode/tasks.json or .githooks/pre-commit) AIDelivery Medium
Detects the artifact-drop stage — git.exe (or the IDE) writing the autoexec files Contagious Interview hides in their fake coding-assessment repos: .vscode/tasks.json (runOn:folderOpen) or .githooks/pre-commit. Opening the workspace or running any git operation afterwards triggers the loader. Rationale: Article explicitly names .vscode/tasks.json (runOn:folderOpen) and .githooks/pre-commit as the two autoexec mechanisms the actor pivots between. Scoping the file write to git.exe / Code.exe / cursor.exe parents narrows from generic IDE noise to clone-time and IDE-write events. Marked hunting because internal repos do legitimately ship tasks.json — pair with UC1 process-spawn alert for full conviction. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1546 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal monorepos that legitimately ship a .vscode/tasks.json
  • Husky / lefthook / pre-commit framework installations writing to .githooks
  • Cookiecutter / project-template generators
  • Cross-team coding-challenge repos cloned by interviewers
  • VS Code 'Configure Default Build Task' creating tasks.json
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any (@"\node_modules\husky\",@"\node_modules\lefthook\",@"\node_modules\@commitlint\"))
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("husky install","lefthook install","pre-commit install"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the contents of the dropped tasks.json or pre-commit file — look for runOn:folderOpen, command/args referencing curl/wget/wscript, or base64 blobs. Pull the repo's git remote origin to identify the GitHub URL and check it against the campaign domain list. 2) Contain: if the file is malicious, quarantine the workspace folder, kill any Code.exe / git.exe descendants on that host, and notify the developer. 3) Hunt: query DeviceProcessEvents for Code.exe spawning shells on that DeviceId in the next 24h (UC1), and DeviceNetworkEvents for traffic to 23.137.105.75:5173 or the Proofpoint domain set. Tag the GitHub repo URL in TI and search inbound EmailEvents for the same URL to identify the original lure.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.vscode\" and FileName =~ "tasks.json")
   or (FolderPath has @"\.githooks\" and FileName in~ ("pre-commit","post-checkout","post-merge","post-clone"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","git-remote-https.exe","code.exe","cursor.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFilePath has @"\.vscode\" and TargetFileName =~ "tasks.json")
   or (TargetFilePath has @"\.githooks\" and TargetFileName in~ ("pre-commit","post-checkout","post-merge"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("git.exe","Code.exe","cursor.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Yeeth-disclosed malicious Jupyter VSIX extensions (ByteBinTools / ToolCraft / OLDev) AIInstallation High
High-fidelity match on the three named malicious VS Code Marketplace extensions Yeeth Security disclosed — they masquerade as Jupyter Notebook productivity tools and beacon via Microsoft Graph API + SharePoint. Catches them at download, file drop, or installed-extension path. Rationale: Direct IOC match against the three exact VSIX names Yeeth Security disclosed in the article. Since the article explicitly cites these as malicious, any hit is high-confidence. Covers both the .vsix bundle file and the unpacked extension folder name VS Code creates under ~/.vscode/extensions/<publisher>.<name>-<version>. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1176 T1036.005 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • None expected — these are exact published-malicious package identifiers
  • Possible benign mention in a security researcher's hunting note file or a blocklist file on disk (low volume; triage by checking file extension and parent process)
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the VSIX hash against the article SHA256 list (35813f44…, c93580…, 4c0d9b…, 62761f38…, d3ebce2f…, 91b9381d…, 6cf9f7b2…, 2812e084…, 52886aab…, d5e9288…, 73469977…, e1bf1b29…, a2b9a769…, bb10adac…, 339907b4…, 808e7154…); pull the workspace/user that installed it. 2) Contain: uninstall the extension via `code --uninstall-extension <publisher>.<name>` on the host, isolate the device, force rotation of GitHub PAT / Azure tokens / browser-stored wallet credentials. Block graph.microsoft.com calls from non-Office binaries at the proxy if feasible. 3) Hunt: search DeviceNetworkEvents for Code.exe-spawned node.exe contacting graph.microsoft.com or *.sharepoint.com from this host; pivot on the user's AAD activity for unusual Graph API consent grants and SharePoint site access.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName matches regex @"(?i)(ByteBinTools\.jupyter-powerdev|ToolCraft\.jupyter-powertools|OLDev\.markdown-mode-devtools).*\.vsix"
   or FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)\\\.vscode\\extensions\\(bytebintools\.jupyter-powerdev|toolcraft\.jupyter-powertools|oldev\.markdown-mode-devtools)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName matches regex @"(?i)(ByteBinTools\.jupyter-powerdev|ToolCraft\.jupyter-powertools|OLDev\.markdown-mode-devtools).*\.vsix"
   or TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)\\\.vscode\\extensions\\(bytebintools\.jupyter-powerdev|toolcraft\.jupyter-powertools|oldev\.markdown-mode-devtools)"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

UNK_DeadDrop Windows VBScript loader → cmd → code.exe --install-extension chain AIInstallation High
Hunts the distinctive Windows infection chain described by Proofpoint — a VBScript launched by wscript.exe spawns a .cmd file which invokes code.exe with --install-extension to sideload the fake-Google VSIX. The wscript→cmd→code chain with install-extension is the smoking gun. Rationale: Article specifies the exact Windows chain: VBScript loader → CMD file → VS Code extension install. `code --install-extension` is the only documented CLI mechanism to programmatically sideload a VSIX, and it being invoked by a cmd.exe whose grandparent is wscript.exe is virtually never benign on an end-user dev workstation. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1059.003 T1176 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Chocolatey / winget post-install batch scripts that bulk-install VS Code extensions
  • Internal IT provisioning scripts (login VBS that sets up dev workstation)
  • Devcontainer setup invoking code --install-extension from a shell
  • Manual `code --install-extension` runs from cmd.exe terminal (no VBS ancestor — would still alert but easily triaged)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("choco","winget","devcontainer","provision"))
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("itadmin","provisioner","sccm"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the VSIX path/name from the --install-extension argument; check it against the three Yeeth IOCs and the article SHA256 list; pull the original VBS file via the wscript.exe InitiatingProcessCommandLine and inspect (look for HTTP fetches, base64). 2) Contain: kill the chain, uninstall the extension (`code --uninstall-extension <id>`), isolate the host, rotate user secrets (browser wallets, GitHub PAT, npm tokens). 3) Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents from this DeviceId for outbound to 23.137.105.75:5173 and the campaign domain list; pivot on Account to find any other host the same user ran a similar chain on; search EmailEvents for the inbound recruitment-themed lure that delivered the original GitHub link.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "code.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--install-extension"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          CodeCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\Code.exe"
| where CommandLine has "--install-extension"
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\cmd.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith @"\wscript.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith @"\cscript.exe"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: VS Code Install-Extension Invoked by VBScript or Cmd Loader (UNK_DeadDrop)
id: 2e9b4d1c-7f3a-4e6b-8d5c-9a2b1d4e7c3f
description: Detects code.exe being invoked with --install-extension from a cmd.exe or wscript.exe ancestor, matching the Proofpoint-described UNK_DeadDrop Windows infection chain that sideloads a fake-Google VSIX.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1059.005
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1176
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\Code.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '--install-extension'
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - DevOps provisioning scripts that batch-install VS Code extensions (rare; usually run interactively)
  - Chocolatey / winget post-install hooks invoking code --install-extension
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\Code.exe OR *\\code.exe) @CommandLine:*--install-extension* @ParentImage:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/code\.exe$/i CommandLine=/--install-extension/i ParentBaseFileName=/^(cmd|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="Code.exe" AND Processes.process="*--install-extension*" AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="Code.exe" AND Processes.process="*--install-extension*" AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime)
UNK_DeadDrop / Contagious Interview C2 callback (23.137.105.75:5173 + Proofpoint domain set) AICommand & Control Medium
Network IOC match for the UNK_DeadDrop C2 endpoint 23.137.105.75 (port 5173 — the Vite dev-server default the actor reuses), sibling IPs 170.205.29.83 / 170.205.30.227, and the 20 Proofpoint-listed campaign domains used for recruitment lures and Overlord C2. Catches the HTTP POST exfil of ZIP files and the live agent traffic on Linux/macOS. Rationale: Article publishes the exact C2 endpoint 23.137.105.75:5173 (port 5173 is Vite's default — a tell that the actor reused dev-tool defaults) plus 20 Proofpoint-listed campaign domains. Direct IOC match is appropriate for alerting tier given the named, attributed infrastructure. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platforms or VT/URLScan integrations resolving the IOCs from a SOC workstation
  • Researcher / IR analyst manual investigation traffic
  • Honeypot or sandbox VMs in the org reaching out
  • Mistyped legitimate domains (very low — these are random-string lures)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("VTUploader.exe","urlscan.exe")) // exclude TI tooling
| where not (DeviceName startswith "SOC-" or DeviceName startswith "IR-") // exclude analyst workstations
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcessFileName making the call — Code.exe / node.exe / Overlord binary on Linux/macOS, or any process beaconing to port 5173. Pull the bytes_out volume to estimate whether ZIP exfil already happened. 2) Contain: sinkhole the IP+domain set at the proxy/firewall, isolate the host, and assume browser-wallet / credential / GitHub token compromise — rotate everything reachable from the device. Pull and preserve %TEMP% ZIP files (Windows pipeline uploads then cleans up). 3) Hunt: tag the IPs/domains in TI and run a 30-day lookback across DeviceNetworkEvents and DNS; search EmailEvents for inbound mail containing GitHub URLs to repos that resolved to this infrastructure; check user's browser history for the GitHub lure URLs.
let c2_ips = dynamic(["23.137.105.75","170.205.29.83","170.205.30.227"]);
let c2_domains = dynamic(["empowerpharmacy.space","nxlog.tech","ondofinance.tech","valorecuiting.online","migadyn.info","contacttrixauvex.ink","trixauvex.org","pulsynk.org","mailtrixauvex.ink","mailpulsynk.xyz","mailpredicttogether.ink","predicttocareer.space","onoplanoai.ink","trixauvexnet.ink","recruitvex.us","nowurisch.fit","hyperdevpipline.org","nemesistrade.work","ceronet.work","deep-ai-guard.store"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (c2_ips)
   or (isnotempty(RemoteUrl) and RemoteUrl has_any (c2_domains))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2_ips = dynamic(["23.137.105.75","170.205.29.83","170.205.30.227"]);
let c2_domains = dynamic(["empowerpharmacy.space","nxlog.tech","ondofinance.tech","valorecuiting.online","migadyn.info","contacttrixauvex.ink","trixauvex.org","pulsynk.org","mailtrixauvex.ink","mailpulsynk.xyz","mailpredicttogether.ink","predicttocareer.space","onoplanoai.ink","trixauvexnet.ink","recruitvex.us","nowurisch.fit","hyperdevpipline.org","nemesistrade.work","ceronet.work","deep-ai-guard.store"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationIP in (c2_ips) or DestinationHostName in (c2_domains) | project TimeGenerated, src=SourceIP, dest=DestinationIP, host=DestinationHostName, port=DestinationPort, proc=DeviceProcessId, table_="CommonSecurityLog"),
  (DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name in (c2_domains) | project TimeGenerated, src=ClientIP, dest=Name, host=Name, port=tostring(QueryType), proc="dns", table_="DnsEvents"),
  (ImWebSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DstIpAddr in (c2_ips) or DstHostname in (c2_domains) | project TimeGenerated, src=SrcIpAddr, dest=DstIpAddr, host=DstHostname, port=tostring(DstPortNumber), proc=ProcessName, table_="ImWebSession")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: UNK_DeadDrop C2 Network Indicators
id: 5d8c2a9b-1e4f-4a7c-8b3d-2f6e9c1a4b5d
description: Detects DNS or network connection to UNK_DeadDrop / Contagious Interview C2 infrastructure disclosed by Proofpoint (23.137.105.75:5173 plus 20 campaign domains).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1041
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:

    DestinationIp:
      - '23.137.105.75'
      - '170.205.29.83'
      - '170.205.30.227'
  domain_match:
    DestinationHostname:
      - 'empowerpharmacy.space'
      - 'nxlog.tech'
      - 'ondofinance.tech'
      - 'valorecuiting.online'
      - 'migadyn.info'
      - 'contacttrixauvex.ink'

(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3) AND ((@DestinationIp:(23.137.105.75 OR 170.205.29.83 OR 170.205.30.227)) OR (@DestinationHostname:(empowerpharmacy.space OR nxlog.tech OR ondofinance.tech OR valorecuiting.online OR migadyn.info OR contacttrixauvex.ink OR trixauvex.org OR pulsynk.org OR mailtrixauvex.ink OR mailpulsynk.xyz OR mailpredicttogether.ink OR predicttocareer.space OR onoplanoai.ink OR trixauvexnet.ink OR recruitvex.us OR nowurisch.fit OR hyperdevpipline.org OR nemesistrade.work OR ceronet.work OR deep-ai-guard.store)))
(#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 OR #event_simpleName=DnsRequest) (RemoteAddressIP4=/^(23\.137\.105\.75|170\.205\.29\.83|170\.205\.30\.227)$/ OR DomainName=/(empowerpharmacy\.space|nxlog\.tech|ondofinance\.tech|valorecuiting\.online|migadyn\.info|contacttrixauvex\.ink|trixauvex\.org|pulsynk\.org|mailtrixauvex\.ink|mailpulsynk\.xyz|mailpredicttogether\.ink|predicttocareer\.space|onoplanoai\.ink|trixauvexnet\.ink|recruitvex\.us|nowurisch\.fit|hyperdevpipline\.org|nemesistrade\.work|ceronet\.work|deep-ai-guard\.store)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_ports values(All_Traffic.app) as proc values(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("23.137.105.75","170.205.29.83","170.205.30.227") OR All_Traffic.dest_host IN ("empowerpharmacy.space","nxlog.tech","ondofinance.tech","valorecuiting.online","migadyn.info","contacttrixauvex.ink","trixauvex.org","pulsynk.org","mailtrixauvex.ink","mailpulsynk.xyz","mailpredicttogether.ink","predicttocareer.space","onoplanoai.ink","trixauvexnet.ink","recruitvex.us","nowurisch.fit","hyperdevpipline.org","nemesistrade.work","ceronet.work","deep-ai-guard.store")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.dest_port) as dest_ports values(All_Traffic.app) as proc values(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest IN ("23.137.105.75","170.205.29.83","170.205.30.227") OR All_Traffic.dest_host IN ("empowerpharmacy.space","nxlog.tech","ondofinance.tech","valorecuiting.online","migadyn.info","contacttrixauvex.ink","trixauvex.org","pulsynk.org","mailtrixauvex.ink","mailpulsynk.xyz","mailpredicttogether.ink","predicttocareer.space","onoplanoai.ink","trixauvexnet.ink","recruitvex.us","nowurisch.fit","hyperdevpipline.org","nemesistrade.work","ceronet.work","deep-ai-guard.store")) by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.dest_host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Axios follow-up malicious npm packages installed (redeem-onchain-sdk / nicegui / period-newline) AIDelivery High
OpenSourceMalware flagged three secondary-payload npm packages dropped within 18 hours of the Axios takedown — redeem-onchain-sdk@1.0.7, nicegui@0.1.4, period-newline@0.1.0 — listed as dependencies of fake cryptocurrency trading-bot GitHub repos. Detects install via file write to node_modules paths or explicit npm/yarn/pnpm install command lines. Rationale: OpenSourceMalware specifically named these three npm packages (with versions) as the post-Axios secondary payloads. Scoping by node_modules path scopes to npm (the PyPI nicegui is a different, legitimate project) and the exact package names give near-zero FP. Worth alerting tier given the article explicitly attributes them to a North Korea-aligned actor. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.007 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer cloning a repo for reverse-engineering / IOC research that legitimately pulls these packages
  • Cached node_modules in a sandbox VM under analysis
  • Defender quarantine restoring artifacts to a sample-analysis folder
  • Internal forks of the malicious package retained for study
Suppression filter
| where not (DeviceName startswith "MALWARE-" or DeviceName startswith "SANDBOX-")
| where not (InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("researcher","malware-analyst"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the host's project root (parent of the node_modules folder) and the source registry — `npm view` the version installed; pull the package's `scripts.postinstall` and `index.js` for analysis. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill any running node.exe / npm processes, rotate every secret accessible from this dev workstation (GitHub PAT, npm tokens, AWS keys, browser-stored wallets, SSH keys); audit the developer's other repos for the same dependency. 3) Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound from node.exe / npm.exe to non-registry IPs (especially 23.137.105.75 and the campaign domains); search npmrc / yarn.lock / pnpm-lock.yaml files across the fleet for the three package names; pivot on the GitHub repo URL declared as `repository` in the package.json to find the lure project.
union
  ( DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]node_modules[\\/](redeem-onchain-sdk|nicegui|period-newline)[\\/]"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, FolderPath, FileName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, EventKind="FileWrite" ),
  ( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") or FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe"))
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("redeem-onchain-sdk","period-newline")
        or (ProcessCommandLine has "nicegui" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm ","yarn ","pnpm ","install"," i ","add "))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath=tostring(""), FileName,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, EventKind="ProcessExec" )
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]node_modules[\\/](redeem-onchain-sdk|nicegui|period-newline)[\\/]"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Malicious npm Package Install (Axios Follow-up — UNK_DeadDrop Adjacent)
id: 9f3a1c7b-4e2d-4b8a-9c5f-3d1e7a2b4c8d
description: Detects file writes to node_modules paths for the three OpenSourceMalware-flagged npm packages dropped as secondary payloads after the Axios takedown by North Korea-aligned actors.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/north-korean-hackers-are-turning.html
author: detection-engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\node_modules\redeem-onchain-sdk\'
      - '\node_modules\nicegui\'
      - '\node_modules\period-newline\'
      - '/node_modules/redeem-onchain-sdk/'
      - '/node_modules/nicegui/'
      - '/node_modules/period-newline/'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - PyPI nicegui (legit Python framework) — not affected; this rule scopes to node_modules so npm-only
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\redeem-onchain-sdk\\* OR @TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\nicegui\\* OR @TargetFilename:*\\node_modules\\period-newline\\* OR @TargetFilename:*/node_modules/redeem-onchain-sdk/* OR @TargetFilename:*/node_modules/nicegui/* OR @TargetFilename:*/node_modules/period-newline/*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/[\\\/]node_modules[\\\/](redeem-onchain-sdk|nicegui|period-newline)[\\\/]/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as filepath values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\redeem-onchain-sdk\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\nicegui\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\period-newline\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/redeem-onchain-sdk/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/nicegui/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/period-newline/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as filepath values(Filesystem.process_name) as proc from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\redeem-onchain-sdk\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\nicegui\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\node_modules\\period-newline\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/redeem-onchain-sdk/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/nicegui/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/node_modules/period-newline/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("23.137.105.75", "170.205.29.83", "170.205.30.227") or RemoteUrl has_any ("empowerpharmacy.space", "nxlog.tech", "ondofinance.tech", "valorecuiting.online", "migadyn.info", "contacttrixauvex.ink", "trixauvex.org", "pulsynk.org", "mailtrixauvex.ink", "mailpulsynk.xyz")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["23.137.105.75", "170.205.29.83", "170.205.30.227"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["empowerpharmacy.space", "nxlog.tech", "ondofinance.tech", "valorecuiting.online", "migadyn.info", "contacttrixauvex.ink", "trixauvex.org", "pulsynk.org", "mailtrixauvex.ink", "mailpulsynk.xyz"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:

    product: windows
detection:

        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'

falsepositives:

level: critical

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("empowerpharmacy.space", "nxlog.tech", "ondofinance.tech", "valorecuiting.online", "migadyn.info", "contacttrixauvex.ink", "trixauvex.org", "pulsynk.org", "mailtrixauvex.ink", "mailpulsynk.xyz")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("23.137.105.75", "170.205.29.83", "170.205.30.227")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
