| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] INFINITERED trojanization — unexpected modification of REDCap PHP system files · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] REDCap webserver process spawning shell / DB client — cookie-driven INFINITERED backdoor · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Exchange/Compliance content rule 'Patroit' with external Gmail BCC (UNC6508) · [LLM] Outbound mail BCC'd to UNC6508 actor dropbox BebitaBarefoot774@gmail.com · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Exchange/Compliance content rule 'Patroit' with external Gmail BCC (UNC6508) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects creation or modification of an Exchange transport / DLP compliance rule that BCCs matching mail to an external personal Gmail address — the exact exfiltration TTP UNC6508 used (rule name 'Patroit', BCC target BebitaBarefoot774@gmail.com). Catches the rule-creation moment, before any mail is rerouted. Rationale: Pivots on the two highest-fidelity strings in the article — rule name 'Patroit' and BCC address 'BebitaBarefoot774@gmail.com' — both confirmed by GTIG's defense-industrial-base writeup. Catches the rule-creation event itself so the SOC can revoke the rule before exfil begins. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/threats-to-defense-industrial-base • https://www.theregister.com/research/2026/06/15/google-says-prc-linked-spies-hid-in-medical-research-networks-for-more-than-a-year/5254547
ATT&CKT1114.003 T1567 T1098.002
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT admin restoring an old backup of compliance rules where 'Patroit' is a typo for 'Patriot' (unlikely but possible)
  • Security team intentionally seeding a 'Patroit' rule as a canary detection
  • M&A activity where an acquired tenant ships rules with personal Gmail BCCs for legacy reasons
  • Authorized DLP rule that BCCs to a Gmail-hosted custody mailbox
Suppression filter
and not (AccountObjectId in ("<dlp-canary-admin-objectid>")) and not (Raw has "DLP_CANARY_TEST")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull the full rule definition (Get-TransportRule / Get-DlpComplianceRule). Confirm BCC target, regex keyword list, and the admin account + IP that created it. Cross-check the admin's recent SigninLogs for residential-proxy / unusual ASN signals. Step 2 — Contain: Disable the rule immediately (Disable-TransportRule), do NOT delete yet (preserve for IR). Force MFA re-enrol and revoke sessions on the creating admin account. Block the external recipient domain at the connector. Step 3 — Hunt: Pull 90 days of OfficeActivity for any other Set/New rules from the same admin, search EmailEvents for any message sent to BebitaBarefoot774@gmail.com or similar Gmail aliases, and pivot to the on-prem REDCap server file integrity for INFINITERED PHP trojanization.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where Application in~ ("Microsoft Exchange Online","Office 365 Security and Compliance","Microsoft Purview")
| where ActionType in~ ("New-TransportRule","Set-TransportRule","Enable-TransportRule","New-DlpComplianceRule","Set-DlpComplianceRule","New-DlpCompliancePolicy","Set-DlpCompliancePolicy")
| extend Raw = tostring(RawEventData)
| where Raw has_any ("Patroit","BebitaBarefoot774")
   or (Raw has "BlindCopyTo" and Raw has "@gmail.com")
   or (Raw has "BlindCopyTo" and Raw has "@outlook.com" and Raw has "Patroit")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, ActionType, ObjectName, Raw
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| where OfficeWorkload in ("Exchange","SecurityComplianceCenter")
| where Operation in~ ("New-TransportRule","Set-TransportRule","Enable-TransportRule","New-DlpComplianceRule","Set-DlpComplianceRule","New-DlpCompliancePolicy","Set-DlpCompliancePolicy")
| extend Params = strcat(tostring(Parameters), " ", tostring(EventData), " ", tostring(ItemName))
| where Params has_any ("Patroit","BebitaBarefoot774")
   or (Params has "BlindCopyTo" and Params has "@gmail.com")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, ClientIP, Operation, ItemName, Params
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound mail BCC'd to UNC6508 actor dropbox BebitaBarefoot774@gmail.com AIActions on Objectives High
Catches any mail sent or BCC'd to the actor-controlled Gmail dropbox UNC6508 used to receive exfiltrated REDCap research mail. Even though Google has disabled the account, the recipient address remains a high-fidelity historical-hunt anchor and would catch operator reuse of the same alias. Rationale: BebitaBarefoot774@gmail.com is named directly by Bleeping/GTIG as the BCC sink for the 'Patroit' compliance rule. Even though Google disabled the account, looking backwards 90-365 days surfaces historical exfil and any operator who recycled the alias. Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security team intentionally sending a canary email to BebitaBarefoot774 to test the detection
  • An end user copying the IOC into a phishing-report email body (matches if the search is too greedy on body content)
  • Threat-intel automation forwarding the IOC list internally as text
Suppression filter
and not (Subject has_any ("IOC report","Threat intel digest","abuse report")) and not (SenderFromAddress endswith "@<your-soc-tooling-domain>")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Treat ANY hit as a confirmed data-exfil incident until proven otherwise. Pull message bodies via Compliance Center eDiscovery; identify subject lines and attachments. Step 2 — Contain: Revoke sessions on the sending mailbox owner, force password reset + MFA re-enrol, search OfficeActivity for the Patroit compliance rule (UC1) on the same tenant. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on SenderMailFromAddress — anything BCC'd to BebitaBarefoot774 was likely matched by the Patroit regex set, so review the same mailbox's outbound flow for adjacent sensitive material that bypassed the rule. Notify research-data owners and execute breach-disclosure workflow for any matched medical/military research content.
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(365d)
| where RecipientEmailAddress =~ "BebitaBarefoot774@gmail.com"
   or tostring(AdditionalFields) has "BebitaBarefoot774"
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, EmailDirection, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation
| order by Timestamp desc
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(365d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "Exchange"
| where Recipients has "BebitaBarefoot774" or P2RecipientList has "BebitaBarefoot774" or EventData has "BebitaBarefoot774"
| project TimeGenerated, Operation, UserId, MailboxOwnerUPN, Subject, Recipients, P2RecipientList, ClientIP
| order by TimeGenerated desc

INFINITERED trojanization — unexpected modification of REDCap PHP system files AIInstallation Medium
Detects writes / overwrites to PHP files under REDCap install directories by a process that is not the documented REDCap upgrade tooling. INFINITERED's recursive-dropper persistence works by injecting into REDCap core PHP files during the upgrade process, so any out-of-band PHP file write on a REDCap server is high signal. Rationale: Pivots on the article's claim that INFINITERED 'trojanizes server system files' and intercepts the REDCap upgrade pipeline (GTIG: 'recursive dropper'). PHP file writes under /redcap/ from non-upgrade-tooling processes is the closest detectable proxy for the trojanization step. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/threats-to-defense-industrial-base • https://www.theregister.com/research/2026/06/15/google-says-prc-linked-spies-hid-in-medical-research-networks-for-more-than-a-year/5254547
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1554 T1574.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • REDCap admin performing a manual minor-version patch via FTP / SCP / WinSCP (drops .php files via session daemon, not composer)
  • Local plugin / hook developer editing PHP under /redcap/plugins/
  • Backup-restore operations replaying a tar/zip extraction via a process not in the allowlist
  • CI/CD deploy job using ansible/saltstack module names that don't match the composer-or-git filter
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\redcap-upgrade\","/opt/redcap-deploy/")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer install","composer update","git pull"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Hash the modified PHP file (SHA256) and compare against the vendor-shipped REDCap checksum for the running version. Diff the file content against a clean copy — look for added eval/base64_decode/preg_replace-with-e-modifier, HTTP cookie parsing (`$_COOKIE[`), or SQL writes to credential tables. Step 2 — Contain: Quarantine the host (DeviceIsolation), pull a memory + filesystem image, restore the affected PHP file from a known-good source. Reset all REDCap database credentials and force re-authentication of all REDCap users. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on the writing process — was it a webshell (php-fpm/apache spawned shell — see UC4)? Search all REDCap servers in the estate for the same SHA256. Cross-check tenant for the Patroit compliance rule (UC1).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\redcap\","/redcap/","redcap_v")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("composer.phar","composer.exe","git.exe","rsync","msiexec.exe","webdeploy.exe","deployer.exe","tar.exe","unzip.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "php.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer","install_redcap","upgrade_redcap"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\redcap\\","/redcap/","redcap_v")
| where TargetFileExtension =~ "php"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("composer","composer.phar","git","git.exe","rsync","msiexec.exe","webdeploy.exe","tar","unzip")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: INFINITERED Trojanization of REDCap PHP System Files
id: 3c7e1f82-9b4d-4a6e-8c2f-1d9a5e7b3c64
description: Detects writes or overwrites of PHP files under REDCap install paths by processes that are not part of the documented REDCap upgrade tooling — the persistence pattern of UNC6508's INFINITERED malware.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/chinese-hackers-breach-redcap-servers-steal-medical-research/
  - https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/threats-to-defense-industrial-base
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/15
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1554
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\redcap\'
      - '\redcap_v'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.php'
  filter_legit_tools:

      - '\git.exe'
      - '\rsync.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\webdeploy.exe'
  condition: selection_path and selection_ext and not filter_legit_tools
falsepositives:
  - REDCap version upgrade run by an admin from an undocumented tool
  - Site-local plugin development
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 OR source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH) (@TargetFilename:(*\\redcap\\* OR */redcap/* OR *redcap_v*) OR @file.path:(*\\redcap\\* OR */redcap/* OR *redcap_v*)) (@TargetFilename:*.php OR @file.path:*.php) -@Image:(*\\composer.phar OR *\\composer.exe OR *\\git.exe OR *\\rsync.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe OR *\\webdeploy.exe) -@process.executable.path:(/usr/bin/composer OR /usr/bin/git OR /usr/bin/rsync OR /usr/bin/tar OR /usr/bin/unzip)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| regex("(?i)(\\\\redcap\\\\|/redcap/|redcap_v)", field=TargetFileName)
| TargetFileName=/\.php$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/(composer|git|rsync|msiexec|webdeploy|tar|unzip)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_hash) as hashes from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.action=created OR Filesystem.action=modified OR Filesystem.action=renamed) (Filesystem.file_path="*\\redcap\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/redcap/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*redcap_v*") Filesystem.file_name="*.php" by host Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | search NOT process_name IN ("php.exe","composer.phar","git.exe","rsync","msiexec.exe","webdeploy.exe") | table firstTime, lastTime, host, file_path, file_name, process_name, user, hashes
REDCap webserver process spawning shell / DB client — cookie-driven INFINITERED backdoor AICommand & Control Medium
INFINITERED's backdoor receives commands via HTTP cookies on REDCap page loads and can execute shell commands and arbitrary SQL. Detects php-fpm / apache / nginx / w3wp spawning a shell, SQL client, or recon binary — the observable surface of cookie-driven command execution. Rationale: Bleeping article spells out the backdoor's capabilities (shell exec, arbitrary SQL, file up/download) and that commands arrive via HTTP cookies on REDCap page loads — meaning each cookie command will surface as a webserver process spawning a shell or DB client. The parent process whitelist is the high-fidelity anchor: php-fpm shouldn't shell out in a healthy REDCap deployment. Cross-checked against: • https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/threats-to-defense-industrial-base
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004 T1059.001 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Scheduled mysqldump backup invoked by the REDCap cron user (parent=php-fpm if called via REDCap cron module)
  • Admin diagnostics page that legitimately runs `whoami` / `id` to surface effective user
  • REDCap module that shells out to ImageMagick / pandoc for report rendering (rare but exists in custom builds)
  • Monitoring agent embedded as a PHP plugin invoking curl for healthchecks
Suppression filter
and not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--defaults-extra-file","backup-redcap.sh","healthcheck")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "/redcap/cron.php")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Capture the full process tree (parent grandparent of php-fpm, child process command line) and the contemporaneous IIS / Apache / nginx access log entry — match by process ID + timestamp. The access log will show the originating IP and the cookie header. Step 2 — Contain: If the cookie header includes a non-session cookie with a base64 or hex payload, treat as confirmed backdoor — isolate the host, preserve memory, and disable the REDCap site. Block the source IP at the perimeter. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot on the source IP across the estate (other REDCap endpoints? other web apps?). Hunt UC3 file-modification on the same host. Pull the last 90d of OfficeActivity for any Patroit-style compliance rule on the same tenant (UC1).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","apache2","nginx","nginx.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","whoami.exe","whoami","id","net.exe","net1.exe","wmic.exe","mysql.exe","mysql","mysqldump.exe","mysqldump","psql.exe","psql","curl.exe","curl","wget.exe","wget","certutil.exe","nslookup.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName !in~ ("systemd","supervisord","services.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
  (SecurityEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where EventID == 4688
   | where ParentProcessName has_any ("w3wp.exe","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe")
   | where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","wmic.exe","mysql.exe","mysqldump.exe","certutil.exe","nslookup.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Source="WindowsSecurity"),
  (Syslog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
   | where Facility == "authpriv" or ProcessName has_any ("auditd","audispd")
   | where SyslogMessage has_any ("php-fpm","apache2","nginx","httpd")
   | where SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/usr/bin/bash","/usr/bin/mysql","/usr/bin/mysqldump","/usr/bin/curl","/usr/bin/wget","/usr/bin/whoami","/usr/bin/id")
   | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SyslogMessage, Source="LinuxAuditd")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: REDCap Webserver Process Spawning Shell or DB Client (INFINITERED Cookie Backdoor)
id: 5d8e2f74-3a1c-4b9f-8d6e-7c2a4f9b1e58
description: Detects php-fpm / apache / nginx / w3wp spawning cmd / powershell / bash / mysql / curl — the observable surface of UNC6508 INFINITERED's HTTP-cookie-driven backdoor on a REDCap host.
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

logsource:

  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\w3wp.exe'
      - '\php-fpm.exe'
      - '\php-cgi.exe'
      - '\php.exe'
      - '\httpd.exe'
      - '\nginx.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/(w3wp|php-fpm|php-cgi|php|httpd|apache2|nginx)(\.exe)?$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|whoami|net|net1|wmic|mysql|mysqldump|certutil|curl|wget|nslookup)\.exe$/i OR ImageFileName=/\/(bash|sh|dash|zsh|whoami|id|mysql|mysqldump|psql|curl|wget)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("php-fpm","php-fpm.exe","php.exe","php-cgi.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","apache2","nginx","nginx.exe") Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","whoami","whoami.exe","id","net.exe","wmic.exe","mysql","mysql.exe","mysqldump","mysqldump.exe","psql","psql.exe","curl","curl.exe","wget","certutil.exe") by host Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | table firstTime, lastTime, host, user, parent_process_name, process_name, cmdlines

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01

description: |

references:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or SHA1 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or MD5 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or SHA1 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86") or MD5 in~ ("ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ba6b73b0ca0dc7f86b3b397893ac32d729fd53f9df20643288f141f29d020af7", "db65c1b9f9e4cb4d729f45ad4b6fcf3e277caf9eb4c875425dec93fd883f9136", "c1ac43d23f89d41eb4ff131678ab562ab2cfed9aa334b13767ef141d303b0e5b", "8f0158855a656b629ca76ebca565f18bc25563ded34b65d6771632c20edb68ec", "51a57bfc9ed3eb6451c1c289607814d59e1698c666fb97ac5f694c398f23d045", "4efbef69eb3b09bacff892d6a55778d07c418e7f15eba3cf1245e8cdfd8dda0b", "58bb25777e0aa86bcd2125101e0bca4e8732b03d91bd8d2f205b446a2a8d5c86"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

    - attack.t1555.003

logsource:

    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'

            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'

            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027

    - attack.defense-evasion

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'

Popular WordPress Plugin Scripts Tampered to Plant Hidden Backdoors on Sites

The Hacker News
2026-06-15 10 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

An attacker tampered with trusted JavaScript files used by WordPress sites running PushEngage, OptinMonster, and TrustPulse, turning those files into a way to break into the sites. When a site administrator was logged in as the file loaded, the code created an admin account under the attacker's control and installed a hidden plugin that opened a way back in. Ordinary visitors did not trigger it

CVEsCVE-2026-10795
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1190 T1195.002 T1555.003
Domainstidio.cc pushengage.com
IPs84.201.6.54

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Tampered PushEngage SDK fetched from clientcdn.pushengage.com during exposure window
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] WordPress PHP process spawning shell from wp-content directory · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Popular WordPress Plugin Scripts Tampered to Plant Hidden Backdoors on Sites
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Rogue WordPress admin account created matching developer_api1 / dev_xxxxxx · [LLM] Suspicious WordPress plugin folder created (content-delivery-helper / database-optimizer)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound traffic to tidio.cc or 84.201.6.54 (Awesome Motive supply-chain C2) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Outbound traffic to tidio.cc or 84.201.6.54 (Awesome Motive supply-chain C2) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects WordPress-hosting endpoints contacting the Sansec-published C2 destinations (tidio[.]cc and 84.201.6.54) used by the tampered PushEngage / OptinMonster / TrustPulse scripts to exfiltrate freshly-minted admin credentials and site metadata. Rationale: Sansec explicitly named tidio[.]cc (registered 2026-04-28) and 84.201.6.54 as the C2 destinations. Both are non-resolvable on a normal WordPress site, so direct IP/domain matches are high-fidelity. Time-bounded to the disclosure window to keep the alert tight. Cross-checked against: • https://sansec.io/research/wordpress-plugin-supply-chain • https://www.pushengage.com/incident-report-june-2026/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher manually visiting tidio[.]cc for IOC validation from a workstation in scope
  • Threat-intel ingestion sandbox detonating the JS payload and replaying the callback
  • DNS resolver retry loop after the domain is sinkholed — duplicate DNS queries from the same host
  • Backup of historical pcap/web-proxy logs being re-indexed and triggering the same network rules
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe") or RemoteIP in ("84.201.6.54")
Response runbook
1. Triage — confirm the source host is a WordPress-hosting endpoint (web server or marketing site) and pull the initiating process / user-agent. Validate the connection was outbound (not inbound scan). 2. Contain — isolate the host, block tidio[.]cc and 84.201.6.54 at the egress proxy / DNS RPZ, and snapshot the wp-content/plugins tree before any cleanup. 3. Hunt — pivot on the host's web-server logs from June 12-14 UTC for inbound POSTs that match wp-admin/admin-ajax.php with previously-unseen action params; enumerate WordPress users for developer_api1 / dev_* and check wp-content/plugins for content-delivery-helper or database-optimizer folders.
let C2Domains = dynamic(["tidio.cc"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["84.201.6.54"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp between (datetime(2026-06-12T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-06-21T00:00:00Z))
| where RemoteIP in (C2IPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains)
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)tidio\.cc(/|$)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let C2Domains = dynamic(["tidio.cc"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["84.201.6.54"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated between (datetime(2026-06-12T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-06-21T00:00:00Z))
| where DestinationIP in (C2IPs) or DestinationHostName has_any (C2Domains) or RequestURL has_any (C2Domains)

Tampered PushEngage SDK fetched from clientcdn.pushengage.com during exposure window AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for endpoints (or web servers acting as origin scrapers) that downloaded pushengage-web-sdk.js or pushengage-subscription.js from clientcdn.pushengage.com between 2026-06-12 and 2026-06-14 UTC, the window in which Sansec observed the tampered script being served. Rationale: The article (and PushEngage's own incident notice) name the two specific JS filenames and the exact CDN host. Bounding the search to 2026-06-12 → 2026-06-14 UTC matches the Sansec-published exposure window so legitimate post-cleanup loads do not trigger. Cross-checked against: • https://sansec.io/research/wordpress-plugin-supply-chain • https://www.pushengage.com/incident-report-june-2026/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1189
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate WordPress site visitors who happened to load the SDK after the CDN cache was already cleared but before stale CDN edge nodes refreshed (PushEngage notes some servers still served it into June 14)
  • Web-scraping monitoring infra (Synthetics, Catchpoint) replaying the URL for availability checks
  • Security researchers downloading both filenames for analysis from corporate workstations
  • Internal CDN-cache invalidation tooling re-fetching the asset to populate replacement copies
Response runbook
1. Triage — confirm whether the downloading endpoint is a WordPress admin browser session (high impact) versus a content-rendering visitor browser (low impact). Pull the SHA256 of the cached JS to compare to PushEngage's clean hash. 2. Contain — if an admin browser loaded the tampered file, force-logout all WordPress administrators on the affected site, rotate WP salts in wp-config.php, and invalidate session cookies. 3. Hunt — pivot to the C2 detection (tidio.cc / 84.201.6.54) for the same DeviceId, enumerate users for developer_api1 or dev_xxxxxx, and inspect wp-content/plugins for content-delivery-helper or database-optimizer folders.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp between (datetime(2026-06-12T00:00:00Z) .. datetime(2026-06-14T23:59:59Z))
| where RemoteUrl has "clientcdn.pushengage.com"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("pushengage-web-sdk.js", "pushengage-subscription.js")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowStart = datetime(2026-06-12T00:00:00Z);
let WindowEnd = datetime(2026-06-14T23:59:59Z);
union isfuzzy=true
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated between (WindowStart .. WindowEnd)
| where (RequestURL has "clientcdn.pushengage.com") and (RequestURL has_any ("pushengage-web-sdk.js","pushengage-subscription.js"))
| project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SrcIP=SourceIP, URL=RequestURL, UserAgent=RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor),
(ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated between (WindowStart .. WindowEnd)
| where (Url has "clientcdn.pushengage.com") and (Url has_any ("pushengage-web-sdk.js","pushengage-subscription.js"))
| project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, SrcIP=SrcIpAddr, URL=Url, UserAgent=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DeviceVendor=EventVendor),
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated between (WindowStart .. WindowEnd)
| where csUriStem has_any ("pushengage-web-sdk.js","pushengage-subscription.js")
| project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIP=cIP, URL=strcat(csUriStem, "?", csUriQuery), UserAgent=csUserAgent, DeviceVendor="IIS")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Rogue WordPress admin account created matching developer_api1 / dev_xxxxxx AIInstallation High
Hunts for the Sansec-published rogue WordPress admin usernames (developer_api1 or anything matching dev_<6char>) appearing in identity / auth / web-server logs. The backdoor JS used the logged-in admin's session to create this account silently. Rationale: Sansec's IoC table explicitly lists 'developer_api1' and the pattern 'dev_xxxxxx' as the rogue admin usernames. These strings should not appear in any legitimate WordPress site's auth or web logs, making string-match detections high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://sansec.io/research/wordpress-plugin-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1098
Data sourcesChange.Account_Management Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate developer accounts coincidentally matching dev_<6char> naming (rare but possible at large hosting providers)
  • Threat-intel feeds / IOC ingestion pipelines emitting the username string in their own log lines
  • Security scanner (Wordfence, Sucuri) producing reports that include the rogue username for awareness
  • WordPress plugins that store the username verbatim in their changelog or admin notice
Response runbook
1. Triage — confirm the source site is one of the affected plugins (PushEngage, OptinMonster, TrustPulse) and pull the wp_users row for developer_api1 / matching dev_* accounts including user_registered timestamp. 2. Contain — delete the rogue admin account, rotate all administrator passwords + WP secret salts in wp-config.php, and invalidate active sessions via wp user session destroy --all. 3. Hunt — check wp-content/plugins for content-delivery-helper or database-optimizer directories, pivot to outbound traffic to tidio.cc / 84.201.6.54, and rotate the CDN API key + database credentials.
union
(DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has @"\wp-content\" or FolderPath has "/wp-content/"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("developer_api1", "dev_")),
(DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("developer_api1", "INSERT INTO wp_users", "wp_insert_user")
  and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)dev_[a-z0-9]{4,8}")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where csUriStem has_any ("/wp-admin/user-new.php","/wp-admin/users.php","/wp-json/wp/v2/users","/xmlrpc.php")
| where csUriQuery has_any ("developer_api1","dev_") or csUriStem has "developer_api1"
| project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIP=cIP, URL=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), Method=csMethod, UA=csUserAgent),
(Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("developer_api1","wp_insert_user")
   or SyslogMessage matches regex @"(?i)\bdev_[a-z0-9]{4,8}\b"
| project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, ProcessName, Message=SyslogMessage),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RequestURL has_any ("developer_api1","/wp-json/wp/v2/users","/wp-admin/user-new.php")
| project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SrcIP=SourceIP, URL=RequestURL, Method=RequestMethod)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WEB

Suspicious WordPress plugin folder created (content-delivery-helper / database-optimizer) AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the Sansec-named hidden-plugin directories that the backdoor installs under wp-content/plugins. These plugin folder names are not associated with any legitimate WordPress plugin and represent the in-tree web shell. Rationale: The article quotes Sansec's IOC list naming exactly two backdoor plugin folders: content-delivery-helper ('Content Delivery Helper') and database-optimizer ('Database Optimizer'). Neither matches any plugin in the WordPress.org repository, so file-create events under those subpaths are nearly noise-free. Cross-checked against: • https://sansec.io/research/wordpress-plugin-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Forensic analyst extracting a tarball of the compromised plugin folder onto a sandbox host for analysis
  • Backup-restore process replaying historical file events into the SIEM after a clean-up
  • Custom internal plugin coincidentally named 'database-optimizer' in a hosting provider's site template (rare — verify by SHA256 against known-good hashes)
  • Wordfence / Sucuri scanner quarantining the backdoor and producing its own file-event records
Response runbook
1. Triage — confirm the host is a WordPress web server and the directory path actually exists on disk. Capture file listing + SHA256 of the PHP files in those folders. 2. Contain — quarantine the entire wp-content/plugins/<folder>/ directory tree (do not delete; preserve for forensics), block the host's egress to tidio.cc and 84.201.6.54, and disable the wp-admin endpoint pending review. 3. Hunt — enumerate wp_users for developer_api1 / dev_* accounts, search for any other PHP files modified in the same minute window across wp-content, and check web-server access logs for the web-shell URL by correlating against subsequent outbound POSTs.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
| where FolderPath matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]wp-content[\\/]plugins[\\/](content-delivery-helper|database-optimizer)[\\/]"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
let Suspicious = dynamic(["content-delivery-helper","database-optimizer"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath matches regex @"(?i)[\\/]wp-content[\\/]plugins[\\/](content-delivery-helper|database-optimizer)[\\/]"
| project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=ActorUsername, FilePath=TargetFilePath, Process=ActingProcessName, Cmd=ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash=TargetFileSHA256),
(Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any (Suspicious) and SyslogMessage has "wp-content/plugins/"
| project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, Actor="", FilePath=SyslogMessage, Process=ProcessName, Cmd="", Hash="")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Sansec hidden WordPress plugin directory (content-delivery-helper / database-optimizer)
id: 7c4d5e6f-3a2b-4c7d-9e1f-2b3a4c5d6e03
description: Detects creation of the hidden-plugin directories installed by the tampered PushEngage / OptinMonster / TrustPulse scripts (Sansec, June 2026). These directories carry the web shell that does not surface in the WordPress dashboard.
references:

author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/15
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1505.003
  - attack.t1195.002
logsource:

      - '/wp-content/plugins/database-optimizer/'

  condition: selection
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.defender) AND (@TargetFilename:(*\/wp-content\/plugins\/content-delivery-helper\/* OR *\/wp-content\/plugins\/database-optimizer\/* OR *\\wp-content\\plugins\\content-delivery-helper\\* OR *\\wp-content\\plugins\\database-optimizer\\*) OR @file.path:(*\/wp-content\/plugins\/content-delivery-helper\/* OR *\/wp-content\/plugins\/database-optimizer\/*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/[\\\/]wp-content[\\\/]plugins[\\\/](content-delivery-helper|database-optimizer)[\\\/]/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.process_name) as process from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/wp-content/plugins/content-delivery-helper/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/wp-content/plugins/database-optimizer/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\wp-content\\plugins\\content-delivery-helper\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\wp-content\\plugins\\database-optimizer\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.user) as user values(Filesystem.process_name) as process from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/wp-content/plugins/content-delivery-helper/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/wp-content/plugins/database-optimizer/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\wp-content\\plugins\\content-delivery-helper\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\wp-content\\plugins\\database-optimizer\\*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
WordPress PHP process spawning shell from wp-content directory AIExploitation Medium
Detects php / php-fpm / php-cgi processes whose working directory or invoking script path resolves under wp-content spawning cmd.exe / powershell.exe / bash / sh — the canonical web-shell execution shape for the hidden Sansec backdoor. Rationale: The article says the hidden plugin opens a web shell — 'anyone who knows the right URL can run code on the server.' On a WordPress host, that materialises as php / php-fpm spawning a shell or curl/wget. Anchoring on the wp-content / wp-admin path eliminates generic PHP CLI scripts. Cross-checked against: • https://sansec.io/research/wordpress-plugin-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress CLI tools (wp-cli) running maintenance tasks that legitimately spawn curl for plugin updates
  • Backup plugins (UpdraftPlus, BackupBuddy) shelling out to tar/gzip from wp-content/uploads
  • Image-processing plugins invoking imagemagick / ffmpeg via shell wrappers
  • Cron-scheduled WordPress jobs that pull remote feeds via curl from wp-content paths
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-cli","updraftplus","backupbuddy","wp-cron.php") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("tar","gzip","rsync"))
Response runbook
1. Triage — capture the full process chain (grandparent → parent → child) and the script path resolved from the PHP CLI args. Identify which WordPress plugin owns the parent path. 2. Contain — kill the offending PHP worker, quarantine the parent script file, and add a temporary egress block for the host to tidio.cc / 84.201.6.54. 3. Hunt — pivot on the same DeviceId for content-delivery-helper / database-optimizer folder writes, rogue developer_api1 / dev_* admin accounts, and inbound HTTP requests for the script path in web-server access logs.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm","php")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash","sh","dash","zsh","nc","ncat","curl.exe","wget.exe")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d", "FromBase64String", "eval(", "system(", "passthru(")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("wp-content","wp-admin","wp-includes")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-content","wp-admin")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|[\\/])php(-cgi|-fpm)?(\.exe)?$"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(^|[\\/])(cmd\.exe|powershell\.exe|pwsh\.exe|bash|sh|dash|zsh|nc|ncat|curl(\.exe)?|wget(\.exe)?)$"
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","FromBase64String","eval(","system(","passthru(")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-content","wp-admin","wp-includes")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-content","wp-admin")
| project TimeGenerated, Host=DvcHostname, Actor=ActorUsername,
          Parent=ParentProcessName, ParentCmd=ParentProcessCommandLine,
          Child=ActingProcessName, ChildCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PHP process spawning shell from WordPress directory
id: 8e5d6f7a-4b3c-4d8e-9a2f-3c4d5e6f7a04
description: Detects php / php-fpm / php-cgi spawning a shell or download utility while running with wp-content/wp-admin/wp-includes in its path or command line — the canonical Sansec backdoor web-shell execution pattern.
references:

  - attack.t1059.001

      - '/php'

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Sniper Dz PhaaS infrastructure delivered via inbound email URLs · [LLM] User click-through on Sniper Dz redirect URL (Safe Links) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS or network egress to Sniper Dz infrastructure (IP and host indicators) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Sniper Dz PhaaS infrastructure delivered via inbound email URLs AIDelivery High
Inbound message contains a URL pointing to known Sniper Dz redirector or landing-page infrastructure (sniperdz.com, raviral.com, win.feezossl.xyz, etc.). Hunts the delivery vector even when the lure was originally posted on Facebook and forwarded to the victim via mail share. Group-IB tied these domains to the post-INTERPOL-takedown resurgence of the kit. Rationale: Uses the specific IOC domains the article enumerates as Sniper Dz infrastructure. Inbound + URL-domain match on a curated list is high-fidelity because these are not generic services; the only FP risk is a security analyst forwarding the IOC list internally.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security analyst forwarding the IOC list or Group-IB write-up via email
  • Threat-intel digest emails that quote the URLs verbatim (Recorded Future, Group-IB newsletter)
  • Phishing-simulation vendor URLs that intentionally mimic these domains for awareness training
  • User reporting the phishing email back through a Report Phish add-in (causes the same URL to traverse the wire again)
Suppression filter
| where SenderFromAddress !endswith "@yourorg.com" and RecipientEmailAddress !in~ ("soc@yourorg.com","phishing-reports@yourorg.com","abuse@yourorg.com")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the full recipient list for the matching NetworkMessageId via EmailEvents and check whether any of them subsequently appear in UrlClickEvents for the same NetworkMessageId — that escalates this from delivery to click-through. Step 2 (contain): soft-delete or quarantine outstanding copies via Defender Threat Explorer for the NetworkMessageId, and add the matched UrlDomain values to the tenant block list. Step 3 (hunt): pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents/DnsEvents on the same domains for the last 14 days across the recipient population to find anyone who opened the URL outside Safe Links (clicked from mobile, copy-pasted into another browser).
let SniperDzDomains = dynamic(["sniperdz.com","raviral.com","offer.raviral.com","win.feezossl.xyz","win.anababayala.com","aff.bnaosf1he.shop","automaticgiveaway.000webhostapp.com","facebookbusiness0078.blogspot.be","dev-cdn370.pantheonsite.io"]);
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
| join kind=inner (
    EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | extend HostLower = tolower(UrlDomain)
    | where HostLower has_any (SniperDzDomains) or Url has_any (SniperDzDomains)
    | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain, ReportId
  ) on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, NetworkMessageId, SenderFromAddress, SenderMailFromAddress, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, DeliveryAction, DeliveryLocation, Url, UrlDomain
| order by Timestamp desc
let SniperDzDomains = dynamic(["sniperdz.com","raviral.com","offer.raviral.com","win.feezossl.xyz","win.anababayala.com","aff.bnaosf1he.shop","automaticgiveaway.000webhostapp.com","facebookbusiness0078.blogspot.be","dev-cdn370.pantheonsite.io"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in~ ("Proofpoint","Mimecast","Cisco","Microsoft")
| where RequestURL has_any (SniperDzDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (SniperDzDomains) or Message has_any (SniperDzDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceUserName, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, Activity, DeviceAction, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc
